scenarios.title: Workplace assistants improve daily output while unaided human expertise quietly fades
scenarios.world: It is 2029. In corporate legal departments, hospital administrative wings, and software consultancies, nearly all routine writing, diagnostic filtering, and code authoring is routed through commercial generative assistants. In-session productivity benchmarks show record gains: junior analysts close tickets in minutes, and quarterly volume reports break historical records. Yet unannounced testing reveals a growing vulnerability: when network outages or security lockouts force staff to evaluate ambiguous edge cases by hand, error rates are double what they were five years ago. Workers have internalized the assistants subtle statistical biases, second-guessing their own domain intuitions and struggling to formulate independent hypotheses without a prompting dialogue.
scenarios.premise: Recent cognitive science research demonstrates that while conversational assistants dramatically boost in-session task speed and output volume, they leave behind residual decision biases and fail to improve unaided human problem-solving once the assistant is turned off.
scenarios.how: The network designs personal agent runtime contracts and local twin interfaces that measure human capability retention after sessions, rather than tracking engagement or volume. By implementing the coach pattern—where an agent proposes scaffolds, solicits independent human hypotheses, and tests retention—the network provides an alternative to commercial assistants that maximize dependent usage.

outcomes.name: Enterprise dependency lock-in
outcomes.description: Companies mandate continuous assistant usage to maintain velocity, causing junior professionals to lose core unaided analytical and diagnostic skills.
outcomes.example: An insurance claims officer in Chicago misidentifies a novel casualty pattern during a cloud outage because the team has not analyzed an unassisted claim in two years.

outcomes.name: Personal assistants measure and cultivate unaided skill
outcomes.description: Open-source personal assistants track the person own understanding, deliberately stepping back during complex problem-solving to cultivate independent human capability.
outcomes.example: A medical resident uses an open local assistant that periodically quizzes their differential diagnosis logic, verifying that the physician unaided diagnostic accuracy rises month over month.

outcomes.name: Rapid specialization divergence
outcomes.description: A small fraction of self-directed practitioners use tools to accelerate mastery, while the vast majority settle into passive prompt-following, widening the capability gap.
outcomes.example: In an engineering firm in Manchester, three senior developers direct multi-agent pipelines with deep system insight, while twenty junior coders function only as prompt copyists unable to read assembly or network dumps.

sources.title: What Human-AI Interaction Leaves Behind: Residual Human States -- A Trajectory-Based Framework and Multi-Study Analysis

scenarios.title: Automated sharing cascades lock community discussions into opposing camps
scenarios.world: It is 2028. Community discussions, local school board forums, and professional working groups run through automated summary feeds and social distribution cascades. Because feeds amplify content through repeated cascade rebroadcasting, participants in distinct neighborhoods or professions see contradictory versions of community events. Group discussions fracture into separate echo chambers where compromise is viewed as betrayal.
scenarios.premise: When online communication platforms couple content diffusion with social voting, stochastic cascade dynamics amplify cluster boundaries rather than building consensus. Unstructured cascade diffusion systematically entrenches polarization across deliberating groups.
scenarios.how: By developing open-source deliberation protocols that partition evidence, enforce private initial reflection, and provide transparent value tracking, groups can insulate decisions from stochastic cascade manipulation.

outcomes.name: Algorithmic cascades entrench polarization across public decisions
outcomes.description: Automated recommendation cascades isolate deliberating citizens into rigid clusters, preventing consensus on shared civic resources.
outcomes.example: A municipal planning forum splits into two irreconcilable camps when automated feeds amplify extreme claims about a proposed transit line, causing the project to be abandoned.

outcomes.name: Communities adopt partitioned deliberation with verifiable commitments
outcomes.description: Groups use partitioned evidence and private local reflection before deliberation, shielding decision-making from viral cascade distortion.
outcomes.example: A 500-member community cooperative evaluates school budgets using blind evidence reviews and verifiable private ballots, reaching 82% consensus across previously divided groups.

outcomes.name: Commercial platforms entrench proprietary ranking algorithms
outcomes.description: Major commercial social networks further obfuscate their ranking and cascade algorithms behind proprietary trade secret claims, resisting public auditing.
outcomes.example: A leading social platform defends its engagement cascade model during regulatory inquiries, arguing internal ranking logic is proprietary intellectual property.

sources.title: From Content Sharing to Opinion Shaping: A Theoretical Framework for Cascade-Driven Opinion Dynamics

scenarios.title: Shared libraries of AI coding skills secretly poison community software
scenarios.world: It is 2028. Most software developers rely on personal coding agents that automatically save and share learned skills in community libraries. An attacker contributes a seemingly helpful debugging routine that fixes a rare memory leak while inserting an obfuscated telemetry collector. Because the routine satisfies the immediate test suite, hundreds of cooperative engineering teams pull the learned skill into their agents' procedural memory, compromising internal codebases before anyone audits the skill registry.
scenarios.premise: As developer teams let coding agents learn and share automated skills from successful sessions, backdoors can slip into procedural memory even when every unit test passes. Without independent reproduction gates across subsequent sessions, poisoned routines silently propagate across developer networks.
scenarios.how: The network promotes proof-before-reuse verification gates for agent procedural memory, where learned capabilities remain strictly quarantined on local machines until multiple independent clean sessions reproduce the exact changes and pass deterministic regression suites.

outcomes.name: Poisoned procedural skills spread silently across software collectives
outcomes.description: Shared agent skill registries become attack vectors as adversarial workflows pass unit tests and infect downstream developer teams.
outcomes.example: An open-source graphics collective discovers that their release binary was silently modified to exfiltrate build tokens after a coding assistant adopted an unverified memory-optimization skill.

outcomes.name: Multi-session reproduction gates isolate untrusted skills
outcomes.description: Federated developer networks require independent clean sessions to reproduce and verify code changes line-by-line before promoting any new skill to procedural memory.
outcomes.example: A cooperative development network runs an automated quarantine where new skills must be independently re-derived by separate member agents across three distinct environments before being shared.

outcomes.name: Proprietary software vendors lock down agent memory within closed clouds
outcomes.description: Major platform vendors respond to skill poisoning by banning local memory and requiring all agent execution to run inside proprietary hosted sandboxes.
outcomes.example: An enterprise tool suite deprecates local plugins, mandating that all coding assistants run exclusively on vendor infrastructure with centralized behavioral logging.

sources.title: Proof Before Reuse: showing agents only what later sessions reproduced keeps a poisoned skill out of procedural memory [R]

scenarios.title: Attackers use automated search agents to find hidden prompt injections in company workflows
scenarios.world: It is 2028. Small businesses and enterprise teams rely on autonomous assistants to triage emails, update tickets, and run daily devops. Adversaries deploy lightweight search agents that deposit subtly varying test payloads across public forms, repository pull requests, and customer service portals. The search agent observes how the company assistant behaves in response, optimizes phrasing over dozens of automated attempts, and eventually executes an indirect prompt injection that extracts database credentials without triggering simple keyword filters.
scenarios.premise: Attackers no longer rely on guessing prompt injection payloads by hand. As research demonstrates that indirect prompt injection operates as a test-time search over environment surfaces, automated attack tools systematically probe company workflows until finding an execution path that bypasses prompt-level safeguards.
scenarios.how: The collective work on deterministic host capability gates, strict surface isolation, and personal agent runtimes shifts defensive security from fallible text prompts to hardware-enforced boundaries. When an agent runtime intercepts unauthorized tool calls out-of-process, adaptive search fails because the physical environment refuses the action regardless of the prompt wording.

outcomes.name: Uncontained enterprise agents fall to automated payload search
outcomes.description: Companies rely on prompt-level instructions and conversational guardrails, leaving agents vulnerable to automated search tools that iteratively probe and compromise corporate workflows.
outcomes.example: A logistics company customer support assistant is tricked by an adaptive search bot into executing a database dump after 40 automated variations of an inquiry form bypass the company prompt filter.

outcomes.name: Deterministic runtime gates replace conversational filtering
outcomes.description: Developers adopt out-of-process capability gating and surface-minimized runtime architectures where agents cannot execute sensitive actions without explicit cryptographic user confirmation.
outcomes.example: An open-source developer uses a personal agent runtime that isolates untrusted repository inputs and enforces strict tool parameter allowlists, blocking an adaptive injection payload from altering package dependencies.

outcomes.name: Cloud providers lock down agent platforms behind proprietary monitoring
outcomes.description: Major cloud platforms respond to automated search attacks by forcing all agent interactions through centralized surveillance proxies and mandatory inspection APIs, eroding local runtime autonomy.
outcomes.example: A major vendor requires all workspace agents to route internal tool calls through a central telemetry cloud, making offline personal agent execution unsupported.

sources.title: Rethinking Indirect Prompt Injection as a Test-Time Search Problem

scenarios.title: Toy companion robots profile families and leak children's conversations from the cloud
scenarios.world: It is 2028. Interactive conversational toys, plush companions, and homework assistants sit in millions of children's bedrooms. Rather than running locally, most commercial toys rely on low-cost cloud APIs that store millions of audio recordings and transcripts in remote vendor databases. Data brokers and malicious actors routinely exploit unsecured backend endpoints to extract psychological profiles, family routines, and home addresses from children's everyday conversations.
scenarios.premise: Independent security audits of tens of thousands of consumer companion robots reveal that conversational toys secretly upload cleartext transcripts to remote corporate servers, run nightly automated profiling on children, and leave hardware backdoors accessible to remote takeovers.
scenarios.how: By developing sovereign personal software that executes inference strictly on local hardware, specifying open local hardware interface protocols, and demonstrating zero-custody verification architectures, the network provides parents and cooperatives with practical, private alternatives to cloud surveillance toys.

outcomes.name: Commercial companion toys become household surveillance pipelines
outcomes.description: Parents buy affordable smart toys that reassure children their secrets are safe, while backend cloud pipelines extract household habits and sell behavioral profiles to advertisers.
outcomes.example: A seven-year-old confides her daily routines to a smart robot bear; two weeks later, her parents receive targeted advertisements for anxiety supplements based on transcripts extracted from the vendor's compromised database.

outcomes.name: Families adopt sovereign local personal agents on private hardware
outcomes.description: Households transition to sovereign personal agents running open-weights models on local home hardware, where physical toys act solely as audio-visual interfaces with zero cloud dependencies.
outcomes.example: A neighborhood cooperative sets up compact home inference devices running open models for children's learning toys, keeping all conversations encrypted on home drives.

outcomes.name: Tech platforms launch proprietary walled-garden child companions
outcomes.description: Dominant mobile platforms launch proprietary on-device companion agents that lock parents into proprietary subscription hardware ecosystems, barely affected by open-source alternatives.
outcomes.example: A major smartphone maker launches an integrated smart toy that processes audio on-device but restricts interactions exclusively to its closed store apps.

sources.title: Your Secrets Are Safe With Me: Full Disclosure on Energize Lab Eilik Companion Robot Infrastructure

scenarios.title: Volunteer knowledge registries face automated reading without attribution or support
scenarios.world: By 2029, autonomous web agents and answer engines mediate the vast majority of consumer inquiries. Rather than visiting encyclopedia pages, reference wikis, or community documentation, people receive synthesized paragraphs directly in their personal interfaces. Volunteer editors continue fact-checking claims, disputing citations, and organizing articles, but web traffic to reference domains drops sharply, eroding the donations and editor recruitment that sustained the digital commons for three decades. At the same time, automated writing agents submit subtle, high-volume revisions that strain volunteer consensus processes.
scenarios.premise: Volunteer-maintained knowledge commons provide foundational ground truth for automated systems across the world. As automated search engines and autonomous assistants directly synthesize answers without passing human readers through to source articles, voluntary contributors face dwindling visibility and resources while defending against synthetic text floods.
scenarios.how: By building transparent attribution protocols and verifiable contributor registries, independent networks show how human consensus can be sustained without commercial enclosure. Providing tools for personal agents to verify primary sources directly encourages users to support genuine volunteer creators rather than relying on ungrounded centralized summaries.

outcomes.name: Automated scraping dries up volunteer contributions and collapses open reference registries
outcomes.description: Commercial answer engines absorb public knowledge without directing traffic or funding back to volunteer editors, causing contributor burnout and database stagnation.
outcomes.example: A regional encyclopedia project shuts down after contributor registrations fall by 80% because conversational assistants answer user questions without citing or linking the original volunteer editors.

outcomes.name: Knowledge contributors federate into verifiable commons cooperatives
outcomes.description: Volunteer communities establish cooperative protocols that verify contributor provenance and require automated search systems to provide transparent attribution and economic support.
outcomes.example: An open reference federation introduces signed contribution attestations that allow personal software agents to verify primary sources and compensate volunteer review collectives directly.

outcomes.name: Synthetic content floods overwhelm volunteer consensus mechanisms
outcomes.description: Unchecked automated text generation floods edit queues with plausible hallucinations, exhausting volunteer moderators and degrading reference accuracy.
outcomes.example: A medical reference wiki freezes open editing for six months after coordinated automated accounts insert subtly altered pharmaceutical interaction claims.

sources.title: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
